checks.label: Continue the pattern of decreasing powers by dividing by the base and it reaches the zero power: on the first screen every stair from 4³ down to 4⁻³ holds the amount of the stair above divided by 4, drawn as that many unit squares or that part of one square, and 4⁰ is one whole square

Any base to the power of zero equals 1 and any base to the power of one is the base itself: on every staircase in the lesson, bases 2, 3, 4, 7 and 10, the stair for power 0 reads 1 and the stair for power 1 reads its base

A negative power gives the reciprocal of the number, 1 over the number: every negative stair reads 1 over the stair of the matching positive power, and is drawn as one part of a square cut into that many

A common misconception is that since the power is negative, the result must be negative, and this is not so: every stair at a negative power reads a positive amount, and its picture always keeps some of the square shaded
Milli is a unit prefix denoting a factor of one thousandth (10⁻³): three steps down from 1 on the stairs of 10 reach 10⁻³ = 1/1000, and the answer is 0.001
Multiplying by 2⁻⁵ divides by 2 five times: the jump on its screen draws 5 hops from 2³ and lands on 2⁻² = 1/4, a quarter of one square
Every line of working on every screen adds up at the number tried, and the first screen's working is right at every power from 3 down to −3
Each puzzle accepts only its right answer, which equals the question at every number tried, while every wrong answer differs, and the right answer's move ends on the stair it names
Before an answer, the marker stays on the start stair with no jump drawn and the stairs below what is known read ?, and a wrong pick draws its own slip, its amount worked out from that pick

Every demonstration has arrived within 5 s of its screen opening, nothing starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, and every step on the first screen within 3 s
